faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 (weeks per year). For a standard full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week. For example, $30/hour × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year. If you work different hours, adjust the weekly figure accordingly.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. On the timesheet, you check a box to add this loading. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05/hour ($26.44 + 25%).

faqs.q: Does the calculator include super and tax?
faqs.a: The calculator estimates super at 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your gross pay, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Tax is estimated using the 2026–27 resident tax rates and Medicare levy (2%). It does not account for HELP loans, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. Always consult a tax professional for your exact situation.

bodyMarkdown:
## Sam Kerr Salary: A Benchmark for Hourly-to-Annual Conversion

When people search for the **sam kerr salary**, they often want to compare a high-profile annual figure to their own hourly wage. While Sam Kerr’s exact pay is not publicly broken down by the hour, the method for converting any annual salary to an hourly rate—or vice versa—is straightforward. This guide explains how to move between hourly and annual pay using the standard 38-hour week, and how to account for casual loading, super, and tax.

## How to Convert Hourly to Annual Pay

The basic formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time employee, we assume 38 ordinary hours per week, as set by the Fair Work Commission. If you work part-time or different hours, substitute your actual weekly hours.

**Example:** At the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, the annual figure is:
$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,254.80

You can also calculate fortnightly pay by multiplying the weekly amount by two. For the minimum wage, that’s $1,004.90 per week, or $2,009.80 per fortnight.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 for a 38-hour week. This applies to award/agreement-free employees. Most workers, however, are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates. Award minimum wages increased by 4.75% from 1 July 2026.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate. On [the timesheet](/) you can check a box to add this loading. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading**—the tool calculates it for you. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour.

## Superannuation: Paid on Top

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer **on top** of your gross pay. It does not come out of your hourly rate. The maximum contribution base for 2026–27 is $270,830, meaning super stops once your earnings exceed that amount. For a minimum-wage worker, super adds about $6,270 per year.

## Tax and Medicare

Resident tax rates for 2026–27 are:
- Nil up to $18,200
- 15% from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this tool’s update. For a minimum-wage earner, total tax and Medicare would be approximately $5,000–$6,000 per year, depending on your situation.

## Using the Timesheet and Pay Guides

[The timesheet](/) is the home page where you enter your base hourly rate. It shows annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures, and includes the casual loading checkbox. For award-specific rates, refer to the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman, which list minimum pay, allowances, and penalty rates for each award.

## Sam Kerr Salary in Context

While the **sam kerr salary** is not publicly disclosed in hourly terms, we can compare it to average earnings. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings in May 2026 were $2,083.70, or about $54.31 per hour. Sam Kerr, as a professional footballer, likely earns well above this average, but the conversion method remains the same: divide her annual salary by 52 weeks and then by her weekly hours to get an hourly equivalent.

## Important Disclaimer

Annual pay shown here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
